cast: One story runs through the book. Zeynep (Ζεϊνέπ), from Izmir, moves to Thessaloniki for work. Her landlady and neighbour is κυρία Κατερίνα; Κατερίνα's son Γιώργος becomes her friend; Σοφία is her colleague at the pharmacy where she works; κύριος Παύλος teaches the evening Greek course; Μάρκο (from Italy) is a classmate. Places: Θεσσαλονίκη, Καλαμαριά, the Λευκός Πύργος, the Χαλκιδική.
grammar_order_check: Each stage lists what it may assume and its set phrases. The order is: letters → είμαι/έχω and the gender of nouns (nominative) → verbs in -ω (present) with δεν and question words → verbs in -άω and -ομαι/-άμαι → the accusative singular and the plural → time and σε + article → review → θα + the perfective stem → the aorist (and the one-past verbs ήμουν, είχα, ήθελα, ήξερα) → possessive and object pronouns, μου αρέσει → review → the B1 additions (passive, reported speech, αν). Anything a dialogue needs earlier is named as a set phrase in that stage's entry.

objectives: Read any Greek word aloud, slowly, with the stress in the right place
Recognise the letters that look Latin but sound different (Η, Ρ, Ν, Υ, Χ, Β, Ρ, Ω)
Read the five spellings of the sound i, and the pairs ου, αι, ει, οι, αυ, ευ, μπ, ντ, γκ, τσ, τζ
Read words Turkish already shares (καφές, χαλί, ταψί) and the numbers 1-10
grammar: spelling and sound: one sound, several spellings (ι, η, υ, ει, οι = i; ο, ω = o; αι, ε = e)
the accent mark: every word of two or more syllables has one, and it is read louder
final ς
set_phrases: Γεια σου! Ευχαριστώ. Παρακαλώ. Ναι / Όχι.
Ένα τσάι, παρακαλώ. (ένα with a neuter noun only; the accusative comes in shopping)

scenario.tr: Zeynep'in Selanik'teki ilk sabahı. Bir kafenin tahtasını okuyor ve çoğu kelimeyi zaten tanıdığını fark ediyor: καφές, τσάι, γιαούρτι, χαλβάς. Garsona üç kelimelik bir siparişi veriyor.
scenario.en: Zeynep's first morning in Thessaloniki. She reads a café's board and finds she already knows most words: καφές, τσάι, γιαούρτι, χαλβάς. She gives the waiter a three-word order.

stages.notes: The other 11 shared words are placed here by the include rule; the chapter lists the ones its text uses. The letter cards of open-alphabet are this stage's drill; the chapter explains the system they drill. Numbers 1-10 are reading practice here and are used from first-words on.

objectives: Greet someone, formally and informally, and say your name
Say where you are from and who you are (είμαι)
Say what you have and what a place has (έχω, έχει)
Ask where something is and understand εδώ / εκεί
grammar: the present of είμαι, all six persons, with the subject pronouns (usually left out)
the present of έχω, all six persons; έχει = there is (a flat has a balcony)
every noun has a gender: ο, η, το (nominative singular only)
assumes: reading: the letters, the accent, numbers 1-10, γεια σου, ευχαριστώ, παρακαλώ
set_phrases: Με λένε … / Πώς σε λένε; / Πώς σας λένε; (λέω comes in everyday-verbs)
Είμαι από την Τουρκία / από τη Σμύρνη (την/τη after από is the accusative: rule in shopping)
Γεια σου / Γεια σας as sen / siz
Στο πάτωμα. (σε + article: rule in getting-around; needed for q-xali-where)

scenario.tr: Zeynep yeni dairesine geliyor. Ev sahibi Katerina Hanım (resmî) ona evi gösteriyor: mutfak burada, banyo nerede, balkon var mı. Merdivende Katerina'nın oğlu Giorgos'la (samimi) tanışıyor.
scenario.en: Zeynep arrives at her new flat. Her landlady, Mrs Katerina (formal), shows her round: here is the kitchen, where is the bathroom, is there a balcony. On the stairs she meets Katerina's son Giorgos (informal).

stages.notes: q-flitzani-drink uses πίνουμε and q-kimas-where uses αγοράζουμε: the chapter glosses them; verbs in -ω come next stage.

objectives: Say what you do every day, and ask others
Conjugate a verb in -ω in the present, all persons
Say no (δεν) and ask with τι, πού, πότε, πώς
grammar: the present of verbs in -ω (γράφω, δουλεύω): -ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν; τρώω and λέω as the two short ones (τρως, λες)
δεν before the verb; questions with τι, πού, πότε, πώς and the Greek question mark ;
assumes: first-words: είμαι, έχω (already the -ω pattern), ο/η/το, με λένε
set_phrases: Μένω στη Θεσσαλονίκη / στην Καλαμαριά (σε + article: rule in getting-around)
Πίνω καφέ / διαβάζω εφημερίδα: an object with no article (the accusative comes in shopping)
Τι δουλειά κάνεις; Πόσο κάνει αυτό; Τι ώρα είναι; (only as questions to recognise, for r-match-questions)

scenario.tr: Balkonda kahve: Giorgos, Zeynep'e ne iş yaptığını, nerede çalıştığını, akşamları ne yaptığını soruyor. Sonra Zeynep, Yunanca kursu için kendi gününü anlatan kısa bir metin yazıyor.
scenario.en: Coffee on the balcony: Giorgos asks Zeynep what she does, where she works, what she does in the evenings. Then Zeynep writes a short text about her day for the Greek course.

objectives: Say which languages you speak, and ask someone to speak slowly
Conjugate μιλάω and its group, and the verbs in -ομαι / -άμαι
Talk about getting up, sleeping, remembering, needing
grammar: the present of verbs in -άω (μιλάω, ρωτάω, ξυπνάω, πουλάω): -άω, -άς, -άει, -άμε, -άτε, -άνε (also -ούν); a tip that some verbs end in -ώ, -είς, -εί (τηλεφωνώ, ευχαριστώ), recognised only
the present of verbs in -ομαι (έρχομαι, χρειάζομαι) and -άμαι (θυμάμαι, κοιμάμαι): all persons; είμαι as the familiar one of this family
assumes: everyday-verbs: verbs in -ω, δεν, question words
set_phrases: Πιο σιγά, παρακαλώ. Δεν καταλαβαίνω. (καταλαβαίνω is a -ω verb; listed as a word)
Τι σημαίνει …; (recognised)
Ξυπνάω νωρίς / κοιμάμαι αργά (clock times wait for getting-around)

scenario.tr: Akşam Yunanca kursunun ilk günü. Öğretmen Pavlos Bey (resmî) öğrencilere hangi dilleri konuştuklarını soruyor; İtalyan Marko ile Zeynep kendilerini anlatıyor. Sonra Zeynep, telefonda Katerina Hanım'a dersin nasıl geçtiğini anlatıyor.
scenario.en: The first evening of the Greek course. The teacher, Mr Pavlos (formal), asks the students which languages they speak; Marko from Italy and Zeynep talk about themselves. Then Zeynep tells Mrs Katerina on the phone how the class went.

objectives: Ask for something in a shop and ask the price
Read opening hours on a shop door
Use the accusative after θέλω, παίρνω, έχετε, and the plural of common nouns
grammar: the accusative singular: τον / την / το, έναν / μια / ένα, and the noun's ending (ο καφές → τον καφέ, η ντομάτα → την ντομάτα); explains the την of Είμαι από την Τουρκία
the plural, nominative and accusative: οι / τα; -ος → -οι, -ας and -ης → -ες, -α and -η → -ες, -ο → -α, -ι → -ια
assumes: first-words, everyday-verbs, more-verbs: the present of all three verb families
set_phrases: Θα ήθελα … (a polite I'd like; the form is not taught)
Πόσο κάνει; / Πόσο κάνουν;
από τις οχτώ ως τις εννιά (opening hours read as numbers; clock time comes in getting-around)
stages.number_table: a table of 11-20 and the tens to 100, taught by the table (no vocab cards), for prices

scenario.tr: Cumartesi sabahı: Zeynep fırında ekmek ve peynirli börek (τυρόπιτα) alıyor, sonra semt pazarında (λαϊκή) domates ve elma. Akşam bakkalın kapısındaki çalışma saatlerini okuyor: pazar kapalı.
scenario.en: Saturday morning: Zeynep buys bread and a cheese pie at the bakery, then tomatoes and apples at the street market. In the evening she reads the opening hours on the grocer's door: closed on Sunday.

objectives: Ask and say the time, and when something happens
Ask the way and understand left, right, straight on
Say where you go and how: στο κέντρο, με το λεωφορείο
grammar: telling the time: Τι ώρα είναι; Είναι δύο. και τέταρτο, και μισή, παρά τέταρτο; στις + number for when (στη μία)
σε + article = στο / στη(ν) / στον / στα / στις / στους: where you are and where you go; με + article for how (με το μετρό)
assumes: shopping: the accusative singular and plural, numbers to 100, the days
the present of all three verb families
set_phrases: Στρίψτε δεξιά. Συνεχίστε ευθεία. (imperatives recognised, not taught)
Θα έρθω στις έξι. (in the listening item l-nikos-time; θα comes in future)

scenario.tr: Zeynep'in ilk iş günü. Durakta bir kadına otobüsün saatini soruyor; eczane Beyaz Kule'ye yakın, nasıl gidileceğini soruyor. Akşam kursa geç kalıyor ve Marko'ya saati soruyor.
scenario.en: Zeynep's first working day. At the bus stop she asks a woman when the bus comes; the pharmacy is near the White Tower, and she asks the way. In the evening she is late for class and asks Marko the time.

objectives: Use everything from reading to getting-around in one longer conversation
See the three verb families and the articles side by side
grammar: a summary table: γράφω / μιλάω / έρχομαι in the present, side by side
a summary table: ο / η / το in the nominative and accusative, singular and plural

scenario.tr: Bir cumartesi: Giorgos, Zeynep'i telefonla arıyor; pazarda buluşuyorlar, otobüsle merkeze gidiyorlar, bir tavernada meze ve köfte söylüyorlar.
scenario.en: A Saturday: Giorgos phones Zeynep; they meet at the street market, take the bus to the centre and order mezes and meatballs at a taverna.

stages.notes: Its words block lists earlier words for revision only (a review stage's words block places nothing). Checks mix all stages.

objectives: Say what you will do, and make plans and appointments
Form the future: θα + the perfective stem
Use the same form after θέλω να / μπορώ να
grammar: the simple future: θα + perfective stem: -ζω/-νω → -σω (θα αγοράσω, θα πληρώσω), -εύω → -έψω (θα δουλέψω), -φω/-πω → -ψω (θα γράψω), -άω → -ήσω (θα μιλήσω); θα είμαι, θα έχω do not change
the irregular futures: θα πάω, θα έρθω, θα φάω, θα πιω, θα δω, θα πω, θα πάρω, θα βρω, θα μπω, θα βγω
θέλω να / μπορώ να + the same form (θέλω να πάω): one short section or a tip
assumes: the A1 stages: the present of all verb families, the accusative, the plural, time and σε + article
set_phrases: Μπορώ να … (μπορώ is recognised as I can; its forms are listed as a word)

scenario.tr: Giorgos, Zeynep'i cumartesi Halkidiki'ye bir günlük geziye çağırıyor. Zeynep'in cumartesi sabahı doktor randevusu var; telefonla randevuyu başka güne alıyor, sonra planı birlikte yapıyorlar.
scenario.en: Giorgos invites Zeynep on a day trip to Halkidiki on Saturday. Zeynep has a doctor's appointment on Saturday morning; she phones to move it, then they make the plan together.

objectives: Say what you did yesterday, last weekend, last year
Form the aorist of regular verbs and know the common irregular ones
Use ήμουν, είχα, ήθελα, ήξερα for the past of verbs that have one past
grammar: the aorist: the future's stem + -α, -ες, -ε, -αμε, -ατε, -αν; the stress moves to the third syllable from the end and a short verb takes έ- (γράψω → έγραψα, γράψαμε)
the irregular aorists: πήγα, ήρθα, έφαγα, ήπια, είδα, είπα, πήρα, βρήκα, μπήκα, βγήκα, έκανα, έμεινα, έμαθα, κατάλαβα
one-past verbs: ήμουν (είμαι), είχα (έχω), ήθελα (θέλω), ήξερα (ξέρω), all persons of ήμουν and είχα
assumes: future: the perfective stem (θα γράψω), the irregular futures
set_phrases: Πώς πέρασες; (περνάω: passed as a set phrase)

scenario.tr: Pazartesi sabahı eczanede iş arkadaşı Sofia, Zeynep'e hafta sonunu soruyor; Zeynep Halkidiki gezisini anlatıyor: erken kalktılar, denize girdiler, bir köyde balık yediler, geç döndüler.
scenario.en: Monday morning at the pharmacy, Zeynep's colleague Sofia asks about the weekend; Zeynep tells her about the Halkidiki trip: they got up early, swam, ate fish in a village, came back late.

objectives: Read a notice from the building manager and a message from a neighbour
Phone the doctor's office and say what hurts
Use my, your, his (το σπίτι μου) and the object pronouns (σε περιμένω, μου αρέσει)
grammar: possessive pronouns after the noun: μου, σου, του, της, μας, σας, τους (το κλειδί μου); the stress moves when the noun is stressed on the third syllable from the end (το τηλέφωνό μου)
object pronouns before the verb: με, σε, τον, την, το, μας, σας, τους (σε περιμένω); μου αρέσει / μου αρέσουν, πονάει το κεφάλι μου
set_phrases: Notices speak in the formal imperative (φέρτε, κλείστε, καλέστε): recognised, not taught
Περαστικά! Χρόνια πολλά!

scenario.tr: Bir hafta, üç metin: yöneticinin asansördeki duyurusu (perşembe su yok), Zeynep'in ateşlendiği gün doktorun muayenehanesine telefonu, ve Katerina Hanım'ın torununun doğum günü partisine davet mesajı.
scenario.en: One week, three texts: the building manager's notice in the lift (no water on Thursday), Zeynep's phone call to the doctor's office the day she has a fever, and Mrs Katerina's message inviting her to her grandson's birthday party.

stages.notes: The include rule places the whole open-everyday-a1a2 pack's remaining items here (notices, the landlord e-mail, the doctor's message, writing and speaking cards); the chapter prepares for them without copying them.

objectives: Tell what happened and what will happen, in one text
Write a short friendly e-mail of 40-60 words, the A2 exam's length
grammar: a summary table: eight common verbs in the present, the aorist and the future
a summary table: the pronouns (εγώ / με / μου …)

scenario.tr: Zeynep, İzmir'deki Yunanca bilen arkadaşı Elif'e Selanik'teki ilk ayını anlatan bir e-posta yazıyor: neler yaptı, ne değişti, gelecek ay ne yapacak. Elif cevap veriyor.
scenario.en: Zeynep writes an e-mail to her Greek-speaking friend Elif in Izmir about her first month in Thessaloniki: what she did, what changed, what she will do next month. Elif replies.

objectives: Understand notices and letters written in the passive
Report what someone said or asked
Say what will happen if …, and join sentences into a 150-word text
grammar: the passive: present -εται / -ονται (ενοικιάζεται, μαζεύονται), aorist -τηκε / -θηκε (γράφτηκε, στάλθηκε), with από for the doer
reported speech: είπε ότι …, ρώτησε αν / πού / πότε …, μου είπε να …; the tense stays as it was said
αν + present or να-form → θα: αν έρθεις νωρίς, θα πάμε μαζί
linking words for B1 texts: επειδή, γι' αυτό, όμως, ενώ, επίσης, στο τέλος (a tip with the exam's writing task)
assumes: all A1 and A2 stages: the present, the aorist and the future of active verbs, the pronouns

scenario.tr: Zeynep belediyeye bir belge için başvuruyor. Memur ona ne getirmesi gerektiğini söylüyor; akşam Giorgos'a memurun ne dediğini anlatıyor (dolaylı anlatım). Apartmanın girişinde bir duyuru: "Το διαμέρισμα 4 ενοικιάζεται".
scenario.en: Zeynep applies for a document at the town hall. The clerk tells her what to bring; in the evening she tells Giorgos what the clerk said (reported speech). A notice in the building's entrance: "Το διαμέρισμα 4 ενοικιάζεται".

stages.notes: Prepares for the open-b1-bridge items (passive, reported speech, conditional forms, the 150-word writing prompts). B1 allows up to 20 minutes of reading.
